classification.difficultyReason: Read roots from factors, average them to locate the axis, substitute for the vertex and sketch each parabola.

content.prompt: Find the $x$-intercepts, the $y$-intercept and the vertex of each parabola and sketch it.

answer.worked:
For the $x$-intercepts, set $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}x(x-4)&=0\\x&=0\text{ or }4.\end{align*}$$
For the $y$-intercept, set $x=0$: $y=0$.
$$\begin{align*}x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{0+4}{2}\\x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=2\\y(2)&=2(2-4)\\y(2)&=-4.\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(2,-4)$ and the parabola opens upwards.

spec.description: Complete equation-driven sketch with intercepts and vertex labelled.

answer.worked:
Set $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}(x-3)(x-2)&=0\\x&=3\text{ or }2.\end{align*}$$
At $x=0$, $y=(-3)(-2)=6$.
$$\begin{align*}x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{2+3}{2}\\x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac52\\y(\tfrac52)&=(\tfrac52-3)(\tfrac52-2)\\y(\tfrac52)&=-\frac14.\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(\frac52,-\frac14)$ and the parabola opens upwards.

answer.worked:
Set $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}2(x+1)(5-x)&=0\\x&=-1\text{ or }5.\end{align*}$$
At $x=0$, $y=2(1)(5)=10$.
$$\begin{align*}x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{-1+5}{2}\\x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=2\\y(2)&=2(2+1)(5-2)\\y(2)&=18.\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(2,18)$. The coefficient of $x^2$ is $-2$, so the parabola opens downwards.

Set $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}2(x-5)(x-6)&=0\\x&=5\text{ or }6.\end{align*}$$
At $x=0$, $y=2(-5)(-6)=60$.
$$\begin{align*}x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{5+6}{2}\\x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{11}{2}\\y(\tfrac{11}{2})&=2(\tfrac{11}{2}-5)(\tfrac{11}{2}-6)\\y(\tfrac{11}{2})&=-\frac12.\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(\frac{11}{2},-\frac12)$ and the parabola opens upwards.

answer.worked:
Set $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}3(x-1)(x+2)&=0\\x&=1\text{ or }-2.\end{align*}$$
At $x=0$, $y=3(-1)(2)=-6$.
$$\begin{align*}x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{-2+1}{2}\\x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=-\frac12\\y(-\tfrac12)&=3(-\tfrac12-1)(-\tfrac12+2)\\y(-\tfrac12)&=-\frac{27}{4}.\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(-\frac12,-\frac{27}{4})$ and the parabola opens upwards.

Set $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}5(x-4)(x+2)&=0\\x&=4\text{ or }-2.\end{align*}$$
At $x=0$, $y=5(-4)(2)=-40$.
$$\begin{align*}x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{-2+4}{2}\\x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=1\\y(1)&=5(1-4)(1+2)\\y(1)&=-45.\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(1,-45)$ and the parabola opens upwards.

Set $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}-6(x-4)(x+3)&=0\\x&=4\text{ or }-3.\end{align*}$$
At $x=0$, $y=-6(-4)(3)=72$.
$$\begin{align*}x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{-3+4}{2}\\x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac12\\y(\tfrac12)&=-6(\tfrac12-4)(\tfrac12+3)\\y(\tfrac12)&=\frac{147}{2}.\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(\frac12,\frac{147}{2})$ and the parabola opens downwards.

answer.worked:
Set $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}7(2x-1)(x+1)&=0\\2x-1&=0\text{ or }x+1=0\\x&=\frac12\text{ or }-1.\end{align*}$$
At $x=0$, $y=7(-1)(1)=-7$.
$$\begin{align*}x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=\frac{-1+\frac12}{2}\\x_{\mathrm{axis}}&=-\frac14\\y(-\tfrac14)&=7(2(-\tfrac14)-1)(-\tfrac14+1)\\y(-\tfrac14)&=7(-\tfrac32)(\tfrac34)\\y(-\tfrac14)&=-\frac{63}{8}.\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(-\frac14,-\frac{63}{8})$ and the parabola opens upwards.
